A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same RAG-3DSG work, with matching methods and experiments. The supplied v2 ends after its references; v3 includes Appendix A.1–A.7. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures support comparison without unresolved reading gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, human evaluations, component ablations, pose-noise experiments and robotic deployment outcomes in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds mechanism comparisons, hyperparameter and density experiments, failure cases and quantitative robot evaluation.

M1.justification: The overall pipeline is retained, but new Algorithm 1 scales the embedding dot product by 1/2 and adds 1/2, whereas Section 3.1 in both versions describes semantic similarity as cosine similarity. Because the pseudocode is presented as documenting the existing mapper, the PDFs do not resolve whether this represents a procedure change or a documentation inconsistency. Newly specified clustering and prompts alone do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use SceneFun3D, FunGraph3D, eight Replica scenes and the indoor robotic deployment. v3 adds analyses and quantitative scoring within this retained coverage. Point-density manipulations change preprocessing and testing procedures without establishing a new dataset, population or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Passive VLM with GPT-4o and GPT-5.2, Re-shot VLM with GPT-4o, and Ours Node + CG Edge as evaluated comparators. Appendix A.4 additionally compares against ConceptGraphs in the existing robot deployment. These substantially expand comparative controls while retaining the original benchmark baselines.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce segmentation-and-merging-only CLIP evaluation, voxel-size and merging-threshold sweeps, single-factor viewpoint scoring, retrieval counts of 1/3/5, unguided refinement and point-density perturbations. Appendix A.4 applies randomized three-expert scoring to robot data. The original benchmark splits, metrics, default hyperparameters and injected pose-noise levels remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained Figure 3 ablations, v3 tests passive model scaling, isolated re-shots and node-versus-edge contributions in Table 1. Appendices A.2–A.5 add hyperparameter sensitivity, retrieval and uncertainty-guidance ablations, density robustness and concrete failure/recovery cases, substantially broadening diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report three annotators, Fleiss' kappa of 0.76 on 100 sampled units and majority-vote resolution. v3 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance-testing procedures; the additional robot evaluation reuses the existing annotation practice.

E6.justification: Existing scores in Tables 1–2 and Figure 3 are retained, but substantial results are added. Examples include isolated Re-shot VLM reaching 59.4% SceneFun3D object R@3, Table 3 reporting mF1 of 28.26/27.66 for top-3/top-5 retrieval versus 30.78 for top-1, and robot node precision of 83.8% versus ConceptGraphs' 65.6%. Further additions include parameter sweeps, density effects and runtime measurements.

T1.justification: The mathematical framework and main Equations 1–3 are retained, and Appendix Equation 4 repeats the voxel-scaling rule. No new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations appear; the added pseudocode principally documents implementation.

C1.justification: The introduction changes 'nearly eliminating' duplicate predictions and hallucinations to 'substantially suppressing' them, and the conclusion replaces 'hallucination-free' with 'less hallucinated'. These meaningfully qualify reliability claims while preserving the central contributions, novelty positioning and state-of-the-art claims.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands explanations of failure conditions and design tradeoffs: misleading bright/transparent re-shots, isolated-render degradation, contextual dilution from additional retrieval, overcorrection without uncertainty guidance, and sparsity-versus-efficiency effects. Section 3.3 also explains the ambiguity-reduction rationale for the retained eight-category relationship taxonomy.

D1.justification: v3 supplies material deferred but absent from the supplied v2: fusion pseudocode, representative prompt templates, factory calibration, 50 ms synchronization, pose interpolation and offline server processing details. It specifies KMeans with K=3 and consensus-score averaging, and reports approximately 0.78 s/iteration for reasoning and 0.26 s/object for rendering. Some few-shot demonstrations remain omitted.

R1.justification: v3 adds PSG-Nav to the introductory navigation citations. The broader related-work discussion and passive-versus-active positioning remain stable. Consolidating the duplicated CLIP reference does not remove a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: v3 substantially expands the explanatory structure through a seven-part appendix containing worked examples, protocol-analysis-conclusion discussions, deployment explanations and annotated prompt templates. The main section order remains stable, with localized rewrites of consensus generation, relationship generation and robustness discussion, plus a new mechanism-analysis paragraph and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains an Analysis block with four comparator rows. v3 adds Figures 5–11, Tables 3–4, Algorithm 1 and multiple boxed prompt templates, substantially expanding visual presentation. Existing principal displays are retained with relocation, running-header changes and small label corrections.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v2's missing supplementary documentation and limited diagnostic support. Explicit implementation information, targeted controls, failure analyses and quantitative robot comparison make the method more reproducible and its evidence more assessable; qualifying the hallucination claims also improves accuracy. Statistical uncertainty remains unreported, some prompt examples are omitted, and the new fusion pseudocode contains a score-normalization ambiguity, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in documentation and validation.
